The interval is the smallest convex set containing $\mathcal A$. This does not assert that its intermediate points are all achievable.

p1-p06.geometry.full-sum.Erdos249257.erdosBorweinMersenneConstant: The full positive-index reciprocal Mersenne sum $E=\sum_{n\ge1}(2^n-1)^{-1}$. Lean defines it as `mersenneTail 0`, the mass remaining before any positive exponent has been processed. Thus it is the largest possible value of a support subsum, obtained by taking every exponent. This definition names the constant, and its irrationality is stated and proved separately.

p1-p06.geometry.digit-injectivity.Erdos249257.positiveMersenneDigitValue_i: The Mersenne digit map is injective, so equal real values imply equality of the entire binary sequences. Coordinate $j$ carries $w_{j+1}$, so the function’s domain `ℕ → Fin 2` includes every positive exponent exactly once. The proof first identifies the positive supports and then each digit. The strict tail inequality prevents the alternative expansions familiar from ordinary binary notation.

Every $x\in\mathcal A$ has exactly one support of positive exponents. The hypothesis `hx : x ∈ mersenneAchievementSet` supplies existence, and injectivity supplies uniqueness. Lean writes “there exists exactly one” as `∃!`. The condition `0 ∉ A` matters because the support value ignores exponent zero, so allowing a free zero coordinate would make literal support uniqueness false.

p1-p06.geometry.coordinate-shift.Erdos249257.mersenneDigitTerm: The contribution of coordinate $j$ is $\varepsilon_jw_{j+1}$, with $\varepsilon_j\in\{0,1\}$. Lean represents a digit by `Fin 2` and casts it to a real number before multiplying. The indexing starts digit coordinates at zero and Mersenne exponents at one. In particular coordinate $0$ contributes the weight $w_1=1$.

p1-p06.geometry.restricted-set.ErdosProblems.Erdos257.supportedMersenne: The achievement set obtained by allowing nonzero digits only at coordinates in $J$. It is the range of `supportedMersenneDigitValue J`, and a permitted digit sequence is zero outside $J$. Here $J$ is a set of zero-based coordinates, so retaining coordinate $j$ retains exponent $j+1$. The definition allows $J$ to be finite, infinite, or empty.

p1-long.thm-supported-dichotomy#1.ErdosProblems.Erdos257.volume_supportedM: If precisely the finite set $F$ of coordinates is forbidden, the restricted achievement set has measure $2^{-|F|}$. The parameter `F : Finset ℕ` lists the omitted zero-based coordinates. The allowed set is its complement. Deleting one coordinate removes one of two disjoint translates of equal measure. Repeating this operation starts from the full achievement set’s measure $1$.

p1-p06.geometry.infinite-omissions.ErdosProblems.Erdos257.volume_supportedM: If infinitely many coordinates are forbidden, the restricted achievement set has Lebesgue measure zero. This is exactly the hypothesis `hJ : Jᶜ.Infinite`. It does not require the allowed set $J$ itself to be infinite. For every $m$, choose $m$ forbidden coordinates. The set then lies inside one of measure $2^{-m}$, and these bounds force measure zero.

p1-p06.geometry.restricted-injective.ErdosProblems.Erdos257.supportedMersenne: The digit map remains injective after restricting the permitted coordinates to any set $J$. The declaration has no finiteness or infinitude hypothesis on $J$. Two restricted digit sequences with the same value are equal because the unrestricted coding is injective. In Lean `Subtype.ext` then converts equality of their underlying digit sequences into equality in the restricted domain.

p1-p06.geometry.restricted-perfect.ErdosProblems.Erdos257.perfect_supported: The restricted achievement set is perfect when the allowed coordinate set is infinite. The hypothesis is `hJ : J.Infinite`, concerning the allowed coordinates, rather than their complement. Any neighbourhood fixes only finitely many digits, leaving another allowed coordinate available to flip. This gives a nearby distinct value. Together with closedness, it proves perfectness. The infinitude hypothesis is essential here.

p2-long.thm-full-support-catalogue#1.Erdos249257.irrational_erdosSum_full_sup: For every integer base $b\ge2$, the sum of all positive-index reciprocals $(b^n-1)^{-1}$ is irrational. p2-long.thm-pairwise-coprime#1.Erdos249257.irrational_erdosSupportSerie: An infinite pairwise-coprime support with summable reciprocals has irrational support series at every integer base $b\ge2$. p2-long.thm-weighted-coeff-engine#1.Erdos249257.irrational_coeff_series_of_w: Under `hgrowth`, the assumption `hcert` supplies a divisibility block, a weighted tail bound and the remaining inequalities for every positive $q$. p2-long.thm-weighted-coeff-engine#1.conc.Erdos249257.irrational_coeff_series_of_w: A natural coefficient sequence $c(m)\le m$ has irrational base-$b$ series if it supplies a weighted block certificate for every positive precision $q$. p2-long.thm-lcm-gap-engine#1.Erdos249257.irrational_erdosSum_of_lcm_g: For a strictly increasing positive exponent sequence, irrationality follows if the next exponent minus the LCM of all preceding exponents tends to infinity. p2-long.thm-factorial-twopow-support#1.Erdos249257.irrational_erdosSum_factoria: The factorial half of the display uses the support given by $(k+1)!$, starting at $1!$. p2-long.thm-factorial-twopow-support#1.Erdos249257.irrational_erdosSum_two_pow_: The series over exponents $2^k$ is irrational at every natural base `hb : 2 ≤ b`. p2-long.thm-multiples-support#1.Erdos249257.erdosSupportSeries_multiples: The support series on multiples of a positive integer $d$ equals the full-support series at base $b^d$. p2-long.thm-multiples-support#1.irration.Erdos249257.irrational_erdosSupportSerie: For `hb : 2 ≤ b` and `hd : 1 ≤ d`, the series restricted to positive multiples of $d$ is irrational. A support periodic at every positive exponent has irrational sum when it contains a positive member. The hypotheses are `hb : 2 ≤ b`, `hm : 0 < m`, positive-index periodicity `hper`, and `hpos`. p2-long.thm-eventually-periodic#1.Erdos249257.irrational_erdosSupportSerie: An infinite support that is periodic above a finite threshold has irrational series at every integer base $b\ge2$. The support of positive exponents congruent to an integer `c : ℤ` modulo `m` has irrational $X_A(b)$, with `hb : 2 ≤ b` and `hm : 1 ≤ m`. p2-long.thm-residue-odd#1.odd.Erdos249257.irrational_erdosSupportSerie: The Mersenne-type series restricted to odd exponents is irrational for every natural base $b\ge2$, recorded by `hb : 2 ≤ b`. p2-long.thm-signed-periodic#1.Erdos249257.irrational_or_bpow_mul_eq_in: For an integer-valued periodic weight and base $b\ge2$, its series is irrational or becomes an integer after multiplication by a power of $b$. p2-long.thm-signed-periodic#1.one-sign.Erdos249257.irrational_intWeightedErdosS: A periodic integer weight has irrational series when its divisor coefficients are nonnegative at positive indices and nonzero arbitrarily far out. Formally, `∀ N, ∃ n, N ≤ n ∧ ExactLocalMersenneHalfRow n` means that the available depths are unbounded. It does not mean that every depth has a row, and it does not require the finite supports for different rows to be compatible. Choosing a larger lower bound gives the paper's convention $n\ge\max(N,1)$. The declaration defines the condition without proving it.

p2-iv.deficit.closed-interval.Erdos249257.upperOrMiddle_within_of_two_: If $s\ge5$, the remainder is at most $2^s$, and $2^k$ times its deficit reaches $2^s$, an upper or middle transition occurs at some $t\in[s,s+k]$. The interval is closed, containing $k+1$ transition indices. The source gives precisely these three premises. Its contrapositive must therefore exclude resets at all those indices, and cannot replace them by a run of only $k$ transitions.

p2-iv.excess.finite-iterate.Erdos249257.affineRightExcess_exactItera: The algebraic identity holds for any integer sequence $X$ and natural pulse sequence satisfying the finite recurrence, not only for this greedy orbit.

p2-iv.late-row.upper-bound.Erdos249257.three_mul_remainder_lt_exact: If $d$ is the largest omitted rank of row $s\ge5$ and $2s<3d$, then $\mathrm{rem}(s)<2^{s+1}+(2\,4^{s-d}+4)/3$. The assumptions are `hs`, `hd` and `hlate`. Lean states the same inequality after multiplication by $3$. The additive error remains present. The result does not give the sharper ceiling $\mathrm{rem}(s)<2^{s+1}$.

p2-iv.boundary.take-threshold.Erdos249257.seamGreedyFloorZ_ne_takeThre: At every row $s\ge5$, the corrected real quotient expression differs from the terminal take threshold. The binder `hs` fixes the row range. Equality would give a finite Mersenne sum equal to $1/2$, contradicting odd denominator parity. This threshold is not the integer value $2^s$, so the theorem does not assert that the centred integer remainder is nonzero.

p2-iv.boundary.zero-permitted.Erdos249257.halfGreedy_skipped_endpoint_: At a real half-greedy skip $s\ge5$, the finite margin is negative, zero, or positive. The hypotheses `hs` and `hskip` identify the row and skip. Negative and zero positions agree with the integer below word, and a positive position agrees with the above word. The zero alternative explicitly permits remainder zero, so this classification cannot be read as a universal nonvanishing theorem.

p2-iv.fatal-gap.sufficient-test.Erdos249257.HalfGreedyFatalGap.skipSafe_: With $u,a>0$ and the skipped-step equality, `hsharp` bounds $u/(2L)$ strictly below `mersenneTailLB3 k`, itself below the full tail. The argument needs no reduced-form or parity conditions on $u,L$.

p2-iv.upper-band.finite.Erdos249257.seamUpperResetDyadicBandEsca: Lean forms the reset charge $E_d$ from four times `overshoot` plus `abovePulse`. The conclusion puts $E_d$ strictly above the upper endpoint or at most the lower endpoint. p2-iv.upper-band.membership.Erdos249257.half_mem_mersenneAchievement: If every eligible upper reset avoids the prescribed dyadic bands, one half belongs to the achievement set. Lean assumes `hband : SeamUpperResetDyadicBandEscape` and concludes membership. The hypothesis quantifies over all upper resets from row thirteen and all their allowed indices. The theorem does not replace this assumption with the finite check through row thirty, and it does not assert that this band condition is necessary for representation.

p2-iv.middle.next-row.Erdos249257.seamMiddleBranch_nextRemaind: A middle transition at row $s\ge5$ yields a successor remainder at least $s+1$. The assumptions `hncarry` and `hmiddle` exclude the upper branch and give the middle inequality. No lower bound on the source remainder is assumed. The conclusion concerns the successor row $s+1$, so it cannot be reused as a bound on the same middle source row without an additional argument.

p2-iv.middle.exponential-next-row.Erdos249257.seamMiddleBranch_nextRemaind: If a middle source row $s\ge5$ has remainder at least $s$, its successor remainder is at least $2^{s+1}+s+1$. The extra premise `hrow` is essential. `hncarry` and `hmiddle` specify the middle transition. This is stronger than the unconditional successor bound by the row index, but it consumes the very source-row lower bound that the membership argument still needs.

p2-iv.middle.row-escape.Erdos249257.SeamMiddleProducerRowEscape: The condition that the source remainder is at least its row index at every middle transition $s\ge13$. Lean lists the absence of an upper carry and the strict middle inequality before the conclusion $s\le\mathrm{rem}(s)$. It is a statement about the source row, not its successor. The declaration defines this unbounded hypothesis. It does not prove it from the branch conditions.
p2-iv.middle.row-escape.Erdos249257.half_mem_mersenneAchievement: If every middle source row from $13$ onward has remainder at least its index, then $1/2$ is represented. The hypothesis `hrow : SeamMiddleProducerRowEscape` requires the bound at all such rows. It controls the producer carry strongly enough to exclude a final middle transition followed by right transitions forever. The bound itself is still an input to the theorem.

p2-iv.middle.sqrt-escape.Erdos249257.SeamMiddleProducerSqrtEscape: The condition that each middle transition $s\ge13$ has producer carry strictly greater than $2\sqrt{2s+2}+4$. The no-carry and middle inequalities appear explicitly in the definition. The square root is taken in the row index $s$, rather than the exponentially larger scale $2^s$. The producer uses the finite below support with rank $s$ inserted. It is not the carry of the infinite greedy support.
p2-iv.middle.sqrt-escape.Erdos249257.half_mem_mersenneAchievement: A producer-carry bound exceeding $2\sqrt{2s+2}+4$ at every late middle row implies half-membership. The argument `hsqrt` is the entire proposition `SeamMiddleProducerSqrtEscape`. The coefficient-tail estimate excludes a last middle transition under this premise. This conditional result does not establish the lower bound on the concrete orbit or convert it into the separate reset-deviation estimate.

p2-iv.last-producer.upper-excluded.Erdos249257.upperProducer_not_last: An upper transition at $D\ge13$ is incompatible with all later row words having terminal digit true. The assumptions `hcarry` and `htrue` encode this configuration, and the conclusion is false. Thus an upper reset cannot be a last producer before an all-right tail. The theorem does not rule out upper resets occurring earlier in a sequence with later non-right transitions.

p2-iv.last-middle.window.Erdos249257.middleProducer_allRight_land: At a middle transition $D\ge13$ followed by an all-right tail, the successor excess is positive and smaller than $2\sqrt{2D+2}+8$. The hypotheses `hncarry`, `hmiddle` and `hright` are all needed. This is a square-root window in the row index. A separate integrality argument improves the lower endpoint to $2$, and nonnegative producer coordinates are not excluded by this upper bound.
p2-iv.last-middle.window.Erdos249257.middleThenAllRight_landingEx: At a final middle row $D\ge13$, the pulse satisfies $p_D^-+2\le4\mathrm{rem}(D)$. With the middle reset identity this makes the successor excess at least $2$. The statement assumes `hncarry`, `hmiddle` and an all-right tail `hright`. It applies only to that final-middle configuration, not to every middle row, and does not exclude larger nonnegative coordinates.

p2-iv.cells.branch-hypotheses.Erdos249257.SeamTwoSidedDyadicCellEscape: The two-sided cell condition prescribes two implications at every row $s\ge5$ without an upper carry. On a middle branch it excludes the signed coordinates $-3,-2,-1$. On a right branch whose overshoot is at most $2^s$, it bounds the upper pulse by $2^{s+2}$. The branch comparisons and the no-carry antecedent are part of the definition. The exclusions are not demands on every row regardless of branch, and the declaration proves none of these conditions.

p2-iv.cells.two-sided-bound.Erdos249257.SeamTwoSidedDyadicCellEscape: Assuming the two-sided cell condition, every row $s\ge5$ has either remainder at most $2^s$ or overshoot at most $2^s$. Lean takes `hescape : SeamTwoSidedDyadicCellEscape`, together with `hs : 5 ≤ s`. At least one of the two bounds holds at each row. The finite base case starts the induction, while `hescape` supplies the branch inequalities needed to continue it at all later rows.

p2-iv.remainder.upper-bound-membership.Erdos249257.SeamGreedyRemainderGapBound: The proposition that $\mathrm{rem}(s)<2^{s+1}$ at every integer greedy row $s\ge6$. It is an upper bound on the remainder itself, not on its distance from $2^s$. The definition carries a universal quantifier over the full late orbit. If supplied, it makes the remainder divided by $4^s$ tend to zero, and finite verified rows alone do not give that limit.
p2-iv.remainder.upper-bound-membership.Erdos249257.half_mem_mersenneAchievement: The unbounded remainder ceiling $\mathrm{rem}(s)<2^{s+1}$ for all $s\ge6$ implies half-membership. The argument `hgap` is precisely that ceiling. Dividing by $4^s$ makes its upper bound tend to zero, and the independently established limit identity identifies the greedy value with $1/2$. The theorem does not establish the ceiling at rows lacking the separate lateness assumptions of other bounds.

p2-iv.capacity.strict-upper-fill.Erdos249257.exists_exactRowStrictUpperFi: A below-half core can be extended to an exact row at depth $2c-2$ if its remaining capacity is less than $2^{c-2}$. The inputs are `hc`, `hD`, `hbelow`, and the sharp inequality `hsharp`. The conclusion produces a finite set $E$ containing $D$, adds only exponents strictly greater than $c$, and states the exact quotient equality. No greedy-prefix identification or critical-crossing hypothesis is required, but the sharp capacity inequality remains an assumption.

p2-iv.capacity.protected-induction.Erdos249257.cofinalExactLocalMersenneHal: The critical quotient supply implies exact rows at unbounded depths. Its input is `hcap : SkippedCoreCriticalQuotientSupply`, a universal inequality for finite cores at critical crossings. The proof iterates a construction from the depth-six seed and shows that the row depths increase. It does not prove `hcap`. A separate equivalence identifies this supply with the inequality along the actual skipped half-greedy prefixes, which is why that reduced condition can be used here.

p2-iv.capacity.protected-progress.Erdos249257.ProtectedExactLocalMersenneR: A finite exact row equipped with an endpoint, cutoff, support and below-half core. Its fields require endpoint at least $6$, cutoff at least $4$, the core contained in the support, new ranks above the cutoff, rank $2$ in the core, and endpoint less than twice the cutoff. These are stored hypotheses of the structure. They make a crossing-based extension increase the endpoint.
p2-iv.capacity.protected-progress.Erdos249257.exists_laterProtectedExactLo: Under critical quotient supply, every protected exact row has a successor protected row with strictly larger endpoint. The inputs are `hcap` and the structured row `s`. The protection data control the locations of new ranks and keep the recycling branch from returning to a smaller endpoint. This theorem supplies genuine progress once the capacity condition is assumed. The ordinary double-or-recycle disjunction alone does not.

p2-iv.capacity.canonical-supply.Erdos249257.HalfGreedySkippedCriticalQuo: The condition that every half-greedy skip at rank $c\ge4$ satisfies the inserted-prefix quotient bound at depth $2c-2$. The definition uses the fixed support `halfGreedyPrefixSupport (c - 1)` with exponent $c$ inserted. The definition quantifies over skipped ranks of this one orbit, rather than allowing an arbitrary core to be chosen at each rank. It states the missing inequality. It does not prove that the greedy prefixes satisfy it.

p2-iv.capacity.one-bit-loss.Erdos249257.localBinarySuffix_two_mul_su: A critical-crossing core at rank $c$ has remaining capacity $S(D,1,2c-2)<2^{c-1}$. The source requires `hc : 4 ≤ c`, `hD` placing the core before $c$, `hbelow` placing its value strictly below one half, and `hskip` making the remaining gap smaller than the weight at $c$. This is the loose bound. It does not supply the sharper bound $2^{c-2}$ used to fill an exact row.

p2-iv.capacity.single-doubling.Erdos249257.exists_exactRowStrictUpperEx: A below-half exact row at $n\ge6$ extends to an exact row at $2n-1$, with all new ranks above $n$. The source explicitly assumes `htwo : 2 ∈ D` as well as `hD`, `hquot` and `hbelow`, and rank-two membership follows separately for exact rows. The conclusion preserves the quotient identity and support inclusion, but does not state that the extended row remains below $1/2$.
p2-iv.capacity.single-doubling.Erdos249257.two_mem_of_exact_localMersen: Supplies the explicit rank-two premise of the extension theorem from exactness. Every exact quotient row at depth $n\ge3$ contains exponent two.

p2-iv.capacity.consecutive-skips.Erdos249257.halfGreedy_precriticalSuffix: If the rational half-greedy rule skips both $c$ and $c+1$ with $c\ge6$, its prefix through $c-1$ has suffix at $2c-3$ smaller than $2^{c-3}$. The hypotheses `hc`, `hskip` and `hnext` state precisely this consecutive-skip configuration. The result is unconditional within that configuration. It does not prove that such configurations occur at unboundedly many ranks.

p2-iv.capacity.pre-take-reduction.Erdos249257.halfGreedySkippedPrecritical: The precritical suffix condition at all skipped ranks is equivalent to requiring it only at skipped ranks $c\ge6$ immediately followed by a take. Consecutive skips already satisfy the bound, and the small initial cases are separately settled. The theorem compares two universal hypotheses. It does not supply the bound in the remaining skip-then-take cases.

p2-iv.capacity.bounded-skip-gap.Erdos249257.halfGreedy_precriticalSuffix: A skip at $c$, followed by $t-1$ takes and then a skip at $c+t$, gives the precritical suffix bound when $0<t\le c-3$ and $c-2\le2^{c-t-3}$. The theorem is uniform in the gap length, but supplies no theorem that the actual orbit has qualifying gaps at unbounded ranks.

The hypothesis `hk` excludes rank zero. The existential quantifier gives a horizon somewhere, with no stated upper bound or relation to $k$. It therefore cannot be used as success by the prescribed horizon $k-2$ without a separate quantitative estimate.

p2-iv.margin.prescribed-horizon.Erdos249257.halfGreedy_precriticalSuffix: For $c\ge4$, the prefix suffix bound at $2c-3$ is equivalent to nonnegative frozen margin at prefix depth $c-1$ and horizon $c-3$. p2-iv.margin.tail-remainder.Erdos249257.HalfCylinderFiniteShadow.bin: Lean proves the finite-window decomposition for every coefficient sequence with $c(n)\le n$, not only the divisor coefficients of a frozen prefix.

p2-iv.margin.linear-tail-majorant.Erdos249257.binaryCoeffTail_le: The bound is uniform for every natural coefficient sequence $c$ with $c(n)\le n$, not just frozen-prefix coefficients.

p2-iv.full-shell.fixed-horizon.Erdos249257.HalfGreedySkippedFullShellNo: The condition that each real half-greedy skipped rank $n\ge3$ has nonnegative frozen margin at prefix $n-1$ and horizon $n$. Thus, with $k=n-1$, the horizon is $k+1$. The definition does not use an unspecified later horizon. p2-iv.full-shell.membership.Erdos249257.half_mem_mersenneAchievement: If the full-shell margin is nonnegative at every real greedy skipped rank from $3$ onward, then $1/2\in\mathcal A$. The argument `hsign` is exactly that universal condition. Its horizon is specified as the skipped rank itself. The theorem needs no sharpening to the earlier precritical horizon for this conclusion, but supplies no proof that its own margin condition holds.

Its conclusion is a conjunction of these facts and equivalences. All are unconditional, but none asserts that arbitrarily late skips exist. The argument `hreturn` is the entire cofinal-return condition. The conjunction in the conclusion contains both infinitude and exact value. p2-iv.live-carry.cofinal-strip.Erdos249257.HalfCarryReachability.infini: A support omitting $0$ and $1$ has infinite support and value $1/2$ if its centred carry is nonnegative and at most $2\sqrt N+4$ at every depth. The assumptions `hzero`, `hone`, `hnonneg` and `hbound` are all stated. For an arbitrary support the nonnegative lower bound cannot be dropped. Greedy-specific theorems later supply it automatically for the actual half-greedy support.

p2-iv.live-carry.future-skip-correction.Erdos249257.halfGreedy_precriticalSuffix: At a rational half-greedy skipped rank $c\ge4$, the precritical suffix bound is equivalent to the live carry at $2c-4$ being covered by future-skip capacity from $c$ over $c-3$ steps. This is an exact reformulation of the precritical test, not an estimate supplying sufficient future skips.

p2-iv.recycling.no-size-gain.Erdos249257.exists_skippedCoreExactRow_o: If a finite support in $[2,n]$ has real value above $1/2$, some crossing rank $4\le c\le n$ produces an exact row at $2c-2$. The assumptions `hE` and `habove` give exactly these bounds and the value inequality. No sharp-capacity hypothesis is required. Since the crossing rank is bounded above rather than below, the new endpoint need not exceed the original endpoint.

p2-iv.recycling.dichotomy.Erdos249257.exactLocalMersenneHalfRow_do: An exact row at endpoint $n\ge6$ yields either an exact row at $2n-1$ or one at $2c-2$ for some $4\le c\le n$. These are `hn` and `hrow`. The disjunction provides one next row, and its alternatives need not be exclusive. It gives no lower bound making the recycled endpoint exceed $n$, and no assertion that doubling can be repeated indefinitely.

p2-iv.recycling.countermodel.Erdos249257.exists_seeded_bounded_double: There exists a predicate with a witness at $6$ and the exact double-or-recycle transition shape, yet with bounded witness depths. The existential predicate is realised by $P(n)\iff n=6$. This proves that the seed and transition shape alone do not imply cofinality. It imposes no assertion on the arithmetic set of actual exact rows, which has additional properties.

p2-iv.certificates.support-criterion.Erdos249257.irrational_erdosSupportSerie: The support series $X_A(b)$ is irrational if weighted coefficient certificates exist for every positive integer $q$. Lean assumes `hb : 2 ≤ b` and `hcert`, which contains the divisibility block, weighted tail bound, positive later coefficient and final inequality. The indices $N,K,L,C$ may depend on $q$. The theorem works for every support and every such base, but does not produce `hcert` for an arbitrary support. At $b=2$ it gives the paper's implication $\mathrm{Cert}(A)\Rightarrow\mathrm{Irrational}(X_A(2))$.

p2-iv.rational-targets.infinite-skips.Erdos249257.rat_mem_mersenneAchievementS: For a nonnegative rational target $q$, representation is equivalent to the greedy rule skipping infinitely many positive ranks. p2-iv.real-targets.reverse-implication.Erdos249257.mem_mersenneAchievementSet_o: A nonnegative target is represented if its greedy rule skips infinitely many positive ranks. p2-iv.finite-support.odd-denominator.Erdos249257.finiteErdosSum_den_odd: Every finite base-$2$ Mersenne sum over a support omitting $0$ has odd reduced denominator. This parity fact excludes finite representations of rationals with even reduced denominator, and passing to an infinite sum requires a separate argument.

p2-iv.reciprocal-mass.dyadic-restriction.Erdos249257.dyadic_support_fraction_reci: If an infinite support has value $p/2^c$, then its reciprocal-index sum diverges or is strictly greater than $1$. The hypotheses `hAinf` and `hvalue` impose infinitude and the dyadic rational value. The numerator `p` is an integer and `c` a natural number. This declaration does not give the same strict conclusion for arbitrary odd factors in the denominator.

p2-iv.zero-windows.logarithmic-bound.Erdos249257.supportCoeffZeroWindow_lengt: If the support contains a positive index and has rational value $p/(2^cv)$ with $v>0$, then each $\varepsilon>0$ admits a constant $B\ge0$ bounding every zero-window length by $\varepsilon\log_2N+B$. The hypotheses `hA`, `hv`, `hvalue` and `hε` are explicit. The constant may depend on the support and parameters. This is an upper bound on window lengths, not existence of long zero windows.

p2-iv.coprime-support.irrationality.Erdos249257.irrational_erdosSupportSerie: An infinite pairwise-coprime support with summable reciprocals has irrational support series at every integer base $b\ge2$. The hypotheses are `hb`, `hA`, `hpair` and `hsum`. Reciprocal summability is a separate assumption from coprimality. In particular, this declaration cannot be applied to all primes merely because distinct primes are coprime. The reciprocal-sum condition must also hold.

p2-iv.bouquet.conditional-irrationality.Erdos249257.SupportSunflowerDichotomy.ir: At base $2$, an orthogonal-petal bouquet support has irrational value if it also satisfies the forced-slot tail-selection condition. The declaration takes two independent assumptions, `hB` and `hselection`. The structural hypothesis controls cores and coprime petals. The selection hypothesis supplies suitable late tails at every required precision. This theorem does not claim that the bouquet structure by itself proves the tail-selection condition.

p2-iv.periodic-support.irrationality.Erdos249257.irrational_erdosSupportSerie: An infinite support that is periodic above a finite threshold has irrational series at every integer base $b\ge2$. The assumptions `hb`, `hm`, `hper` and `hinf` require the base, positive period, eventual periodicity and infinitude. The equivalence in `hper` must hold for every index above the threshold. The theorem therefore allows finite initial changes but does not cover an arbitrary aperiodic tail.

p2-iv.reduced-denominator.error-proof.Erdos249257.irrational_of_den_mul_abs_su: A real number is irrational if rational approximants are eventually unequal to it and their reduced denominators times their absolute errors tend to zero. The assumptions `hne` and `h0` state both requirements. A fixed rational target distinct from an approximant has error at least the reciprocal of the product of their denominators. This domain-neutral theorem needs actual reduced-denominator error control, not a lower bound on denominators.

p2-iv.lcm-gap.sufficient.Erdos249257.irrational_erdosSum_of_lcm_g: For a strictly increasing positive exponent sequence, irrationality follows if the next exponent minus the LCM of all preceding exponents tends to infinity. The assumptions `ha`, `ha0` and `hgap` state these conditions, with `hb` fixing $b\ge2$. The difference is a natural-number subtraction. This criterion is sufficient. It does not claim that every irrational support has such large exponent gaps.

p2-iv.carry.rationality-equivalence.Erdos249257.erdosSupportSeries_rational_: For every support $A$, its base-$2$ value is rational exactly when a positive integer multiplier admits a tempered integer carry orbit for the divisor coefficients. The declaration has no support hypotheses. Temperedness includes the affine recurrence and decay after division by $2^N$. The equivalence identifies the arithmetic object to exclude for an irrationality proof. It does not assert that no such orbit exists.

p2-iv.carry.unique-tempered-orbit.Erdos249257.temperedBinaryOrbit_eq_scale: Every tempered integer orbit for a coefficient sequence bounded by its index equals its multiplier times the exact coefficient tail at each depth. The hypotheses are `hgrowth` and `horbit`. Temperedness removes the exponentially growing homogeneous solution of the recurrence. This identifies any possible integer orbit uniquely, but it does not show whether the resulting real tail values are integers.

p2-iv.carry.common-multiple-lower-bound.Erdos249257.one_add_mul_card_le_two_mul_: If a finite support subset divides $L>c$, the shifted recurrence and positive next state give $1+v|F|\le2u(L-c-1)$. The assumptions `hcL`, `hpos`, `hrec`, `hFA` and `hFdvd` specify those inputs. The strict condition $L>c$ ensures the sampled coefficient is genuinely at row $L$. The theorem uses a lower bound at chosen common multiples, not a global upper bound.

p2-iv.carry.unbounded-positive-orbit.Erdos249257.shifted_state_unbounded_of_i: For an infinite support, any positive natural state sequence satisfying the shifted carry recurrence with multiplier $v>0$ is unbounded. The assumptions `hAinf`, `hv`, `hpos` and `hrec` are explicit. No temperedness or tail identity is required. Unboundedness is compatible with linear growth and with decay after division by $2^n$, so it does not itself contradict a rational-value hypothesis.

For every real $x$ between $0$ and the full Mersenne sum, nonmembership is equivalent to lying in an internal gap determined by a finite prefix and a next rank. p2-v.sources.32.Erdos249257.HalfGreedyTwoThirdsBand.post: A last skip after a take is dyadically unsafe precisely when the preceding reciprocal remainder lies in the stated interval. Lean assumes `hR : 0 < R`, `hRq : R < q`, and `hm : 1 ≤ m`. The interval is $(q(m-1)/(q+m-1),qm/(q+m))$. This is a local equivalence for supplied rational parameters. It does not show that the actual half-greedy orbit ever enters, or always avoids, the interval.

p2-v.sources.33.Erdos249257.HalfGreedyTwoThirdsBand.sing: For a take followed by exactly one intervening skip, dyadic unsafety is equivalent to the reciprocal remainder lying in the two-thirds band. The hypotheses are `hR : 0 < R` and `hRq : R < q`. This specialises the general interval to the next threshold $m=2q+2$. The statement concerns the singleton-skip configuration, and conclusions derived from this band should not be advertised as applying to arbitrary longer runs of skips.

p2-v.sources.34.Erdos249257.HalfGreedyTwoThirdsBand.not_: When both $R$ and the positive $q$ are integers, $R$ cannot lie in the two-thirds band. The assumptions are `hq`, `hRm` and `hqn`. The latter two identify rational parameters with integer casts. The band models the single-skip take–skip–take configuration after a take. This declaration excludes that band only, and interpreting it as a statement about a greedy run requires the corresponding band characterization.

p2-v.sources.35.Erdos249257.HalfGreedyTwoThirdsBand.seve: Positive odd integers $p,D,q$ in the cleared two-thirds band satisfy $p\ge7$. The binders `hp`, `hD`, `hq`, `hpodd`, `hDodd`, `hqodd` and `hband` give all assumptions. The band defect is divisible by four, forcing the numerator bound. This is the singleton take–skip–take specialization. The theorem does not cover every possible length of unsafe skip run or prove reachability of its data.
